proof:
# Cap mass plus section mass is not log-concave, even below the OC budget

The mass equations of a normal cap-cover stress involve, in each cap,
weights W_z=c_z+r S_z, where c_z is its actual d-volume in fiber z,
S_z is its actual section (d-1)-volume, and r>=0 is a multiplier.
The following exact example rules out identifying this law with a
concave-root or log-concave fiber-volume law merely from convexity of
the body and a cap budget below OC. The multiplier is prescribed here;
it is NOT asserted to arise in an actual below-OC minimizing cover.

Let n=1,d=5, let

    K={x in R^5:x_j>=0, sum_j x_j<=1},
    C=[-1,1] x K,
    S={-1,0,1} x K.

This is a convex body with three positive integer fibers of volume1/120,
so M=1/40. Consider the closed ambient cap

    H={L(z,x)>=0},    L(z,x)=3/100-z/100-x_1.

Its continuous normal is the unit vector -e_1. Put

    t_z=97/100+z/100,

so its three values are96/100,97/100,98/100. All three cuts are proper.
The simplex slice formula gives exactly

    c_z=(1-t_z^5)/120,
    S_z=t_z^4/24=5t_z^4/120.                         (1)

There is no orientation normalization hidden in S_z: each section is
in the plane x_1=constant with ordinary Euclidean H_4 measure. The
cap's normalized mixed volume is

    sum_z c_z/M =1406574933/10000000000
                  <3125/15552=(1/2)(5/6)^5.          (2)

The difference in (2) is the positive rational number
146483541281/2430000000000. Thus this is strictly below the exact OC
cap budget for these n,d, not just below one half.

Take r=1/2. Up to the common factor1/120, its cap-plus-section law is

    h(t)=1-t^5+(5/2)t^4.

For 0<t<1, h is positive and direct differentiation yields

    h h''-(h')^2
      =-5t^2(t-1)(t+1)[t^4-4t^3+6t^2-4t+6]
      =5t^2(1-t)(t+1)[(t-1)^4+5]>0.                 (3)

Therefore log h is STRICTLY CONVEX throughout the entire proper-cut
range. In particular the actual three sampled weights violate the
ordinary log-concavity inequality:

    h(96/100)h(98/100)-h(97/100)^2
       =13912864519608719/100000000000000000000>0.    (4)

They also violate every positive-power concavity requirement. Indeed
for every a>0,

    (h^a)''=a h^a[(log h)''+a((log h)')^2]>0,

so h(t)^a is strictly convex on this interval. Its midpoint is strictly
below the average of the other two samples. In particular a=1/d does
not give a concave volume root.

All identities use actual cap volumes and ordinary full section
measures, with no effective trace ambiguity or boundary mass. The
original cap-volume root c_z^(1/5) and section-volume root S_z^(1/4)
retain their respective Brunn--Minkowski concavity properties. Adding
the two dimensional measures with the factor r does not preserve
log-concavity. Any proof needing such a property for a genuine stress
must prove an additional restriction on that stress; the small cap
budget alone is insufficient.
